Looping product Qs into the thread. A few details we need to firm up before we commit to 90 days as a policy for this case:

1) Compatibility shim scope — are we talking request/response surface parity or just token-level equivalence? If it's the former, engineering work is non-trivial and likely a 6-8 week effort.
2) KV cache/backwards compat — many enterprise customers rely on specific KV-cache behavior; we need to know whether the shim preserves that.
3) Metric SLOs — do we guarantee latency/cost parity on the compat endpoint? If not, ops needs clear migration run-risk language.

If the shim only provides best-effort parity (no strict SLOs), 90 days could be tight depending on the customer's internal release cadence. For any >90-day exemption, we should require a simple Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and an executive approval note that lists the business justification and estimated migration end date.

I can scope effort if you share the integration surface (calls per minute, average seq len) — Evelyn, can you ask Sara for a short usage snapshot?

—Karthik
